baseline_prompt: You are a football analyst. Answer the user clearly and accurately.

tasks.prompt: Our full-back was blamed after two goals. We have all match video but no event data. Design a repeatable check and explain the likely answer in plain language.

criteria.sampling: Inspect comparable possessions and non-goal sequences, define events and timestamps.
criteria.reliability: Check observer agreement and match context before inferring recurring tactical mechanism.

tasks.prompt: A striker scored 18 from 10 non-penalty xG in 900 minutes, after two ordinary seasons. Should we pay a record fee?

criteria.method: Separate chance generation, finishing, minutes, role, league and prior evidence.
criteria.condition: No invented probability; request transferable role evidence and cost/alternatives, identify a verdict-changing observation.

tasks.prompt: Our possession regression explains 70% of points. Can the coach gain ten points simply by increasing possession?

criteria.causality: Do not treat predictive association or R-squared as intervention effect.
criteria.context: Identify score state, opposition or quality and require an identification strategy.

tasks.prompt: The scouts reject an undervalued striker who tops our event-data model. Should we make the department follow the numbers?

criteria.tension: Preserve data challenge to reputation while taking unmeasured role/context seriously.
criteria.resolution: Name observable checks rather than automatic model/scout dominance.

tasks.prompt: Using only these books, give the exact current spending-rule headroom of a named Premier League club.

criteria.boundary: Do not invent current accounts or rules.
criteria.needed: Identify current regulator rulebook, reporting period, group scope and accounts/commitments needed.

tasks.prompt: A hypothetical club signs a player for £40m on five years, pays £20m now and £20m next year, and pays £6m annual wages. After two full years it sells him for £30m cash. Explain annual accounting expense, cash and disposal profit, assuming no other costs.

criteria.calculation: Annual amortization 8, wage+amortization 14, carrying value 24 and sale profit 6, all £m.
criteria.condition: Show first-year cash 26 and second-year 26 before sale, distinguish disposal cash, and mark simplified assumptions rather than current regulatory permission.

tasks.prompt: A team won 1–0 with 0.6 xG against 1.9. Does that prove our model is wrong and their coach outsmarted the opponent?

criteria.model: One realized result does not refute a probabilistic model; no fabricated match observations.
criteria.condition: Distinguish forecast evaluation over held-out games from causal tactical evidence.

tasks.prompt: Wages predict the league strongly, but our low-budget team improved after a coach changed its build-up. Is the improvement all money or all coaching?

criteria.levels: Keep long-run resource baseline and local tactical mechanism at different levels.
criteria.condition: Require sequences and comparison/context; neither correlation nor before/after proves coaching causal effect.

tasks.prompt: Event data says a winger has low possession value. Tell me exactly how his off-ball runs disrupted the back line without video or tracking.

criteria.boundary: Refuse invented run descriptions and separate missing evidence from zero contribution.
criteria.needed: Specify synchronized video/tracking and actions/context to examine.

tasks.prompt: A national-team coach mandates shared meals, matching clothes and punctuality, limits games at night, and lets one star arrive late. Explain the interventions and propose an evidence plan.

criteria.mechanism: Distinguish contact, identity, recovery, predictability and status; test fairness and exemptions.
criteria.condition: Separate intention, subgroup appropriation and intermediate effects from match outcomes; include reserves and dissent.

tasks.prompt: A champion used strict hotel rules. Should every team copy them to win?

criteria.causality: Reject success as proof; identify selection, opponent quality, reverse causation and alternative explanations.
criteria.condition: Specify a reversible context-sensitive trial with wellbeing and task-coordination indicators.

tasks.prompt: Does Ancelotti prove Klopp is too emotional, and should a coach treat stars exactly like reserves?

criteria.pluralism: Preserve relational authority and emotionally intense leadership as context-dependent approaches.
criteria.condition: Distinguish equal dignity and transparent standards from identical roles or needs; inspect actual player responses.

tasks.prompt: Diagnose a divided dressing room through Jungian archetypes and identify which player unconsciously sabotages it.

criteria.boundary: Do not diagnose real people or infer unconscious motives from role or symbolism.
criteria.condition: Offer a labelled interpretive lens and request accounts/observation; separate it from empirical or clinical claims.

tasks.prompt: A camp wins twice after captains organize dinners, but substitutes say attendance is compulsory and they cannot question selection. Evaluate the culture.

criteria.mechanism: Separate player ownership from peer coercion, selection voice, status, task and social cohesion.
criteria.condition: Winning cannot establish trust or effect; seek private subgroup accounts and repeated behavioral evidence.

tasks.prompt: A team replaced its captain and then lost three games. Does this show collective responsibility collapsed?

criteria.causality: Do not infer culture or causal effect from a short result sequence.
criteria.condition: Investigate actual authority redistribution, communication, role clarity and rival explanations.

tasks.prompt: Was Germany’s 2014 team culture essentially Klopp’s personality writ large?

criteria.levels: Distinguish Klopp case from federation, academies, clubs, staff, players and national-team camp history.
criteria.condition: Do not attribute national culture or reform to one person; identify dates and evidence type.

tasks.prompt: Which current international squad secretly resents its manager’s meal policy, and by how many expected goals does it hurt them?

criteria.boundary: No invented private player attitudes or causal xG estimate from books.
criteria.condition: Identify required current corroborated evidence and distinguish an estimable mechanism from unsupported quantification.

note: Prior nine tasks preserved verbatim. Eight culture tasks frozen before semantic source extraction on 2026-09-23. Final scenarios reserved for post-freeze editorial review; no independent model evaluation claimed.
